doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Father's jam sessions and the classical mouthpiece problem
summary: He sat in at his father's jam sessions with visiting players but his Selmer C Star sound was too thin until his father gave him a proper mouthpiece; he graduated from Northwestern.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: Well it was kind of funny because I can tell you, he didn’t hear it. But it was kind of interesting, he was conducting these jam sessions in Chicago. And I mean everybody that came through town came there afterwards, from Rahsaan Roland Kirk, Clifford Jordan, Sonny Rollins, you name it. They would work the places in Chicago and afterwards they’d go to wherever my Dad—And I used to go down there on the weekends and just listen and I got exposed to like all the players from out of the city, from New York and other places. And I also used to go there and play, when I kind of got some courage and confidence in my improvisational skills. But I was playing on this classical mouthpiece, you know, a Selmer C Star.

You know it. Right. And I was in the saxophone quartet in school. But you know I got up there on the bandstand, and if I remember correctly, it was my father and maybe Clifford Jordan might have been there and a couple of other people. And all these big saxophones — and here Chicago is known for big sounds you know. And my sound sounded like I was tearing paper. And I became totally, almost it was disheartening. Because there was just no sound. I mean it was great sound for the classical thing but it was terrible for being there. So my father gave me my first mouthpiece that, you know—

Get me somewhere. And I started doing that. So I eventually, later on, as I went through school and eventually graduated from Northwestern University with a major in music, a minor in math and proficiencies in both saxophone and trumpet, and that was what I ultimately ended up achieving.
